## Executive Summary

Litware Terminal Services (LTS) operates a rapidly scaling industrial terminal handling business that grew revenue 31.3% from $45M in FY2024 to $59.2M in FY2025 [1], with a 2026 budget targeting $78M in revenue and $39.5M in EBITDA [2]. The company serves 35 active clients across 38 projects and added 13 new clients in 2025 [3]. Yet the business has **no CRM system** — pipeline management relies entirely on fragmented SharePoint sites, Excel spreadsheets, and individual memory [4][5]. In a company where maintenance terminal handling delivers 55–90% profit margins [6] and clients return annually to quarterly [7], every missed renewal or unidentified cross-sell opportunity represents high-margin revenue leakage.

This paper evaluates the opportunity to deploy an AI-powered CRM with cross-sell intelligence specifically designed for LTS's multi-location enterprise clients. Enterprise customers such as Northlake Energy, Calder Fuels, and Vantera Petroleum operate terminals across Fairview, Bell Harbor, Kenmore, and Ashford, but no systematic mapping exists to identify expansion opportunities across these footprints [8]. Our analysis validates that a properly implemented CRM, combined with AI-driven cross-sell identification, could generate **$3.14M–$5.44M in incremental annual revenue** and **$1.78M–$3.23M in incremental EBITDA** at steady state against the 2026 budget baseline — representing a **2.3–4.1 percentage-point EBITDA margin improvement** on the $78M budget. Implementation costs are estimated at $35.3K–$68K in Year 1, producing a payback period of under 6 months once Phase 1 value is realized.

### Current State

Litware Terminal Services is experiencing rapid growth with significant revenue volatility. FY2025 delivered $59.2M in revenue with $24.1M in EBITDA (40.8% margin), up from $45M revenue and $19.5M EBITDA (43.2% margin) in FY2024 [1]. Revenue is growing at approximately $104,000 per month with high statistical significance (p=0.0011), though a coefficient of variation of 40.4% indicates substantial month-to-month swings [18]. The 2026 budget projects $78M in revenue with $39.5M in EBITDA, implying a 50.7% EBITDA margin [2].

## Implementation Approach

### Technical Requirements

### Timeline

| Phase | Timeline | Scope | Expected Value |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Phase 1: CRM Foundation** | Months 1–3 | Client database migration, bid/proposal tracking, automated follow-up workflows, basic reporting dashboard | Pipeline visibility, 30-day quick win via bid deadline automation. Directly addresses Erin's and Owen's daily pain points |
| **Phase 2: Cross-Sell Intelligence** | Months 4–9 | Enterprise client facility mapping, home-region location database, cross-sell target identification, maintenance contract lifecycle alerts | Systematic identification of expansion opportunities across Northlake Energy, Calder Fuels, Vantera Petroleum, and other multi-location clients |
| **Phase 3: Predictive Analytics** | Months 10–18 | Win/loss tracking and analysis, predictive win-rate modeling by client type/project size/region, integration with fleet scheduling | Data-driven bid prioritization optimizing for highest-margin project selection under capacity constraints |

| Facility/Location Data Provider | $4.25K–$7.1K | Reonomy, D&B Hoovers, or similar for home-region terminal mapping |
| Claude API Integration | $2.55K–$4.25K | Building on Owen's existing workflow; minimal custom development |
| Internal Champion Time | ~10 hrs/week for 3 months | Erin Vaughn (already identified) + Owen Pratt |
| **Total Year 1 Investment** | **$35.3K–$68K** | |
